purpose: Bounded factual review of ten already-written batch-10 articles; article files kept read-only.

sampleSelection.reason: Prioritized GM07A Part 2 encoded/ambiguous oxygen, mixture, rail-pressure and injector rows plus a brake-electronics case.

methods: Captured SHA-256 and modification timestamp for each selected article before review, then verified every hash remained unchanged at completion.
Read each complete article and its JSON source/applicability metadata.
Read page-bounded source text for all cited pages; checked row starts so preceding or following codes were not misattributed.
Rendered and visually inspected 13 original PDF pages; used a higher-resolution row crop for C0506 to confirm small current and timing values.
Compared every numerical threshold, unit conversion, command/operating state and reporting count stated in the sample against the cited main/continuation rows.
Read additional pages 574–576 for P01BF context and checked the supplied assignment's P01BF/P0207/P029D dictionary titles.
Checked that each article retains the unresolved file-to-model/engine applicability boundary and avoids component replacement conclusions unsupported by the monitor.

summary.outcome: No material factual errors found in the ten sampled article versions. This is a bounded sample, not approval of the batch or source calibration.

samplingLimits: Only these ten SHA-256-identified article versions were reviewed; writer10 was still creating other files. No claim is made about unreviewed files or later revisions.
Selection intentionally targeted potentially ambiguous GM07A Part 2 rows; it is not statistically representative of 100 articles.
Thirteen original PDF pages were visually inspected; other cited continuation pages were read as page-bounded text. Visual pages are listed per article.
The application-matrix/download-filename join was not resolved or independently audited here. The review verified that articles preserve that uncertainty and make no vehicle/engine inference.

No vehicle VIN, installed engine, ECU calibration or transmission was verified; no hands-on diagnosis, component testing, complete workshop-tree reproduction, repair recommendation or human mechanic approval is implied.
Referenced lookup tables and source-wide inhibit/enable sheets were not exhaustively audited. Claims are bounded to what each article actually states.
No broad repository tests were run. No batch-10 article was edited.

verifiedClaims: Main P0058 row begins near the bottom of physical page 525; preceding dew-point text belongs to another row.
Bank 2 sensor 2 low-side driver: high voltage during driver ON is the short-to-power signature.
Published impedance is <=0.5 ohm to controller power; decision interval 0.1 second; two-trip reporting.
Page 526 continues heater-release eligibility, completed start, POST DRIVE exclusion, and thermal/dew-point conditions.

findings.description: No material factual error found. The article correctly ties high voltage to the ON command and does not treat impedance as a manual test instruction.

verifiedClaims: The P013C row evaluates bank 2 sensor 2 rich-to-lean transition response.
The filtered result subtracts the exhaust-mass-flow correction from raw time before updating the arithmetic filter.
Correction range 0.04–0.10 second; failure threshold >0.75 second; two counts and one-trip/EWMA reporting.
Primary commanded lambda =1, engine running and eligible speed/flow/stability conditions are required.

findings.description: No material factual error found. Raw and corrected time are kept distinct. The source's malfunction column calls the metric a delay response while its strategy/raw-input description calls it transition response; the article's general response terminology avoids inventing a different metric.
